extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from XML/PDF result text and figure captions. Automated keyword notes were replaced with source-bounded phenotype/morphology claims and an explicit unresolved molecular mechanism limitation.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Subtilin L-Q11 treatment of S. aureus ATCC 29213 is associated with loss of viable counts and O.D.600 decrease after 3 h, supporting a cell-lysis phenotype.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Subtilin L-Q11 against Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 29213

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=22:Subtilin L-Q11 Induced Serious Morphological and Intracellular Changes in S. aureus Cells;fig=5

mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports lysis/killing phenotype, not a resolved molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM images of treated S. aureus cells show time-related surface hollowness, membrane disruption, and cell fragments after exposure to 256 ug/mL Subtilin L-Q11.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Subtilin L-Q11 against Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 29213
mechanism_claims.limitations: Morphology supports membrane damage/cell lysis but does not identify a receptor or molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TEM images show disrupted intracellular organization, cytoplasm leakage, damaged/discontinuous membranes, and ruptured cells after Subtilin L-Q11 treatment.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Subtilin L-Q11 against Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 29213
mechanism_claims.limitations: Morphology supports severe cellular damage but remains downstream evidence, not a resolved molecular mode of action.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper explicitly treats the precise molecular killing mechanism as unresolved and proposes membrane-potential, ATP, conductivity, transcriptomic, and proteomic follow-up studies.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not promote protein-synthesis, nucleic-acid, ATP, or membrane-potential language to direct mechanism claims; those are proposed future work/context.

limitations: No direct receptor, membrane-potential, ATP, conductivity, transcriptomic, proteomic, protein-synthesis, or nucleic-acid mechanism assay is performed in this paper.
SEM/TEM/time-kill evidence supports lysis and membrane/cellular damage only at phenotypic/morphological strength.
